account.title: Sign in with Samsung account
account.description:
1. Open the developer tools of your browser (F12) and switch to the **Console** tab.
2. [Sign in to your Samsung account]({login_url}) in the same tab.
3. At the end, the browser tries to open an address starting with `ms-app://` and fails. Copy that complete address and paste it below. Chrome and Edge show it in the Console as *Failed to launch 'ms-app://…'*; otherwise look for it in the **Network** tab.

Home Assistant then keeps a Samsung account token and creates new SmartThings Find sessions by itself when they expire. Treat it like your Samsung password: anyone with access to your Home Assistant configuration can use it to access your Samsung account.

cookie.title: Samsung SmartTags Setup
cookie.description:
Visit [SmartThings Find]({url}) and log in with your Samsung account.

1. Open Developer Tools in your browser (F12).
2. Navigate to the Application/Storage tab.
3. Copy the **JSESSIONID** value.

*Note: Make sure to copy the one from `smartthingsfind.samsung.com` (you might have others from different domains).*

reauth_confirm.title: SmartThings Find session expired
reauth_confirm.description:
Samsung rejected the stored JSESSIONID, so your tags can no longer be updated.

Visit [SmartThings Find]({url}) and log in with your Samsung account.

1. Open Developer Tools in your browser (F12).
2. Navigate to the Application/Storage tab.
3. Copy the **JSESSIONID** value.

*Note: Make sure to copy the one from `smartthingsfind.samsung.com`.*

reauth_account.title: Sign in to Samsung again
reauth_account.description:
Samsung no longer accepts the stored account token.

1. Open the developer tools of your browser (F12) and switch to the **Console** tab.
2. [Sign in to your Samsung account]({login_url}) in the same tab.
3. At the end, the browser tries to open an address starting with `ms-app://` and fails. Copy that complete address and paste it below. Chrome and Edge show it in the Console as *Failed to launch 'ms-app://…'*; otherwise look for it in the **Network** tab.

Home Assistant then keeps a Samsung account token and creates new SmartThings Find sessions by itself when they expire. Treat it like your Samsung password: anyone with access to your Home Assistant configuration can use it to access your Samsung account.
